unclear_spend_kinds:
Redo of a done task, Try again on a failed task's card, and Redo from main on a rebuild or conflict card. These are not a review's send-back, so 'fixes' does not clearly cover them.
- Decision: they count against the same budget. They never reset or raise it.
- Evidence: the same task row is used, and actual_cost_usd_micro is only ever written by task.addCost (packages/state/src/repos/task.ts:104-116) or as 0 on new rows (packages/runtime/src/daemon/plan-tasks.ts:154, session/project-plan.ts:576, jobs/handover.ts:574, :644). A Redo with nothing left pauses before it runs with one card and Continue (executor.ts:977-995). BA-7 keeps such a task one sample.
- Why: the owner's intent is that the budget is what the task costs, and a Redo is that task's work done again.

A retry after a failed run, a transient error retried at once, the ladder's next rung and its stand-in specialist (U-044).
- Decision: they count, as fixes and work.
- Evidence: they are work runs on the same task (runner.ts:933-936; executor.ts:696-706 already subtracts them).
- Why: work done again on the task.

The agent's task check (d1109-selftasks-run, C4), even when one task's report triggered it.
- Decision: it stays out of every task's budget, as the session's spend, paid only from the room after the session's promise (ADR 0119's amendment of 0112). The session review names it apart (BA-8).
- Evidence: its token has no task id and its Run row has task_id null (git show fix/d1109-selftasks-run:packages/runtime/src/session/task-check.ts lines 473-490 and 519-539, session.recordSpend).
- Why: it judges the whole task list and may change other tasks, so the report is only its evidence. Chat's 'fix the tasks' (C6, SC-4) follows the same rule, booked to the project.

The critic's session review, its lesson reviews (promotion) and the monthly calibration.
- Decision: they stay out.
- Evidence: no task id (runner.ts:1159-1176 session token; loop/critic.ts:931-1007; critic.ts:500 taskId only for a task subject; jobs/calibration.ts).
- Why: they review the session, a lesson or known examples, not one task's work.

Planning (intake, Change the plan) and chat answers about a task.
- Decision: they stay out. They count against the project's budget and the monthly cap, as built for owner_questions[1].
- Evidence: intake Run rows have task_id null (session/intake.ts:1914-1921), and conversation tokens carry no task id (conversation/agent.ts:1581-1594).
- Why: not one task's spend. Work that chat starts counts as work.

Web searches inside a work run.
- Decision: they count, as now.
- Evidence: priced into the call's cost (billing/src/pricing.ts:214-231; agent/loop.ts:679-680, :865), so already in the run's cost and the task's figure.
- Why: part of the work. Page reads (web_fetch) book no money.

A review that a budget or credential refused after one or more calls, a review Stop now cut off, and a review that failed.
- Decision: count what it booked. A refusal is still 'no review, no try' (ADR 0112 'leftovers7-session').
- Evidence: its calls are in the ledger with the task id (critic.ts:496-516; hooks.ts:262-283; the cut-off call via agent/loop.ts:765-801, CUT_OFF_STOP_REASON).
- Why: it is the review's spend. BA-3's floor and BA-4's room avoid most of it. BA-7 takes no review sample from such a review.

The critic's project checks and verification tries, the kept-work check after a pause, rebuilds after another merge, conflict handling and the merge step.
- Decision: nothing to count, and no sentence about them.
- Evidence: no model call, nothing booked (loop/critic.ts:640-684: the checks run before the first model call; ADR 0112:511-515; session/dependent-branches.ts:33-60; loop/merge.ts budgetUsdMicro 0 at :1432, :1607, :1989).
- Why: no spend. A Redo they lead to counts as work.

A call Stop now or a timeout cut off, the late usage of a stopped Claude Code run, and an SDK run's subagents.
- Decision: they count, as now.
- Evidence: booked through model_call_end and lateRunCost (executor.ts:1250, :2456-2499; agent/sdk.ts' per-model booking).
- Why: the run's own spend.

Reviews of a task without a budget of its own.
- Decision: no per-task cap. They stay under the session's budget and its review reserve, and the row keeps 'each run stops at CHF 2.40 (the coder's limit)'.
- Evidence: runCapOf's specialist-limit branch (executor.ts:696-706); the owner spoke of 'a task's budget'.
- Why: there is no task budget to count against. Their spend still shows in the row's cost and on Costs.
